title: 'People were screaming in pain' during Co-op Live evacuation
originalTitle: 'People were screaming in pain' during Co-op Live evacuation
content:
Rap music fans who were evacuated from a concert after an unknown substance was released have said there was a "burning" feeling in their throat and they started to "cough and splutter" and some people were "screaming in pain".

Some 12,000 people were evacuated from Co-op Live Arena after the incident at US rapper Don Toliver's show at the Co-op Live in Manchester at about 22:00 GMT on Sunday.

One person was taken to hospital, and more than 80 were assessed by paramedics.

Concertgoers have described feeling "unsafe" and seeing "distressing" scenes and people "coughing up blood", with some claiming the venue's security was lax.

Leon Douzi said he was "right next to" where the substance was released, and "there was this gas coming out of a can" and someone holding it and then "it just hit me in the throat" and it felt like "burning", like pepper spray.

He said it was scary and "there was a bit of panic. Everybody was having the same feeling and trying to get out."

Poppy Rutter and Sophie Billing, both 19, who had travelled from Cambridge to see the concert, said it was not immediately clear what had happened.

Sophie said: "I thought something had gone wrong with smoke coming off stage.

"We started to suffer, coughing and spluttering and feeling tight-chested. A member of staff said it was tear gas.

"Security rushed in and went straight to the pit. We only left as we were starting to feel unsafe and not 100 per cent well."

She said there was "no communication", adding: "You would think Manchester would be extra vigilant, given what's happened in the past."

Jessica Moult-Boffey, 23, of Wigan, said she went to the exit and saw "lads on the bridge" which leads into Medlock Square "crying and screaming in pain".

The music fan added that they were "asking for help" but there were only two stewards outside.

She said she felt "confused on how something like that got into a venue of that size".

Poppy said: "I just cannot believe it.

"When we went in, no-one checked my bag.

"I held it up and said, 'Do you need to check my bag?'

"The security staff member said: 'No, it's okay.'

"Every single other person I spoke to didn't have their bag checked either."

Co-op Live said on its website there were a range of security measures, and while "some of these are visible, others you won't be able to see".

It said the arena used a "frictionless security screening that detects prohibited items without you needing to empty your pockets".
